text:
Customer Rep: FYI — AcmeCorp is seeing intermittent 502s on streaming generate after their token rotation window. They report it started after rotating tokens around 09:12 UTC.
Support Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4583. Tagging #eng-oncall and #support.
Alyssa M: thanks — can you paste a short example of a failing request/response and the SDK they use? streaming or non-streaming?
Customer Rep: streaming only (server->client chunked). They use our JS SDK v0.9.6 with keepAlive enabled. Short log from customer:
```
REQUEST id=abcd1234 POST /v1/stream/generate
AUTH Bearer <rotated-token-1>
RESPONSE 502 gateway error upstream returned 502
CONN reused=true
```
Samir: initial hypothesis: token cache on our edge proxies isn't being invalidated when token rotated by auth service, causing edge to present stale credential downstream and downstream proxy returns 502. This would mostly affect long-lived connections / connection reuse.
Jia: I tried to reproduce locally with a tiny curl loop + HTTP/1.1 keep-alive. Repro steps that hit 502 for me: 
1) Start streaming request with token A.
2) Rotate token in auth service to token B (simulate TTL refresh).
3) New request reuses existing connection pool entry -> edge still using cached token A for upstream handshake -> upstream rejects -> 502 returned to client.
Repro command: 
```
# start long poll stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN_A" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate" &
# rotate token (simulate)
echo "rotate" > /dev/null # token rotation simulated by updating auth cache
# fire second request reusing pool
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN_B" -v --keepalive-time 60 "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate"
```
Samir: logs from edge showing mismatch: 
```
[edge] 2026-03-12T09:12:31Z id=abcd1234 auth_cache_lookup=TOKEN_A
[edge] 2026-03-12T09:12:32Z id=efgh5678 auth_cache_lookup=TOKEN_B
[upstream] 2026-03-12T09:12:32Z id=efgh5678 status=502 reason="auth-mismatch: token invalidated"
```
Eng Oncall: plausible. That explains intermittent nature — only when client connection reuse collides with token rotation window. A couple of immediate mitigation options: 
- server-side: force eviction of auth cache entries on rotation events, or mark in-flight connection metadata to re-validate Authorization header per-request instead of trusting cached token.
- customer-side: temporary workaround: disable keepAlive / connection pooling or restart client process during rotation windows.
Alyssa M: can we do a hotfix to evict token entries on rotation? How fast would that be? Customers impacted: AcmeCorp (high-traffic), BetaApps (low rate).
Samir: small change in edge auth cache: listen to rotation webhook and invalidate matching keys. I can ship a canary to staging in ~90 mins, prod in next deploy after smoke tests. Patch: `edge/auth/cache: add onRotate(key) -> invalidate()`
Jia: tested on staging with simulated rotation webhook — fixed for my reproducer. No regressions in perf tests.
Support Bot: Canary deployment started: canary-id=canary-2026-03-edge-71. Monitoring p95 and 502 count.
Alyssa M: draft customer update (short): 
"Hi — we’re investigating intermittent 502s for streaming after token rotations. Root cause appears to be edge auth cache serving stale token during connection reuse. We’re deploying a canary hotfix that invalidates cached tokens on rotation; expecting roll-forward in ~2 hours. Temporary workaround: restart client process or disable connection pooling during rotation windows. Will update when canary passes"
Samir: rolling canary succeeded on staging, manual smoke looked good. I'll promote to prod after a 30m observation window.
Eng Oncall: after 30m canary in prod, 502 spike dropped to baseline. Observed 0.3% -> 0.01% for streaming 502s for affected customers.
Customer Rep: relaying to AcmeCorp — they asked for ETA; sharing your customer message now.
Alyssa M: postmortem notes to include: token-rotation -> edge auth cache TTL mismatch + connection reuse. Remediation: rotation webhook-based eviction + add unit test for cache invalidation + update SDK docs to mention keepAlive caveat for rotation-sensitive flows.
Support Bot: Incident INC-2026-4583 status=monitoring; owner=Samir; sla-impact=false; next-update=in 60m.
Samir: followups: 1) add metric for auth-cache-hit-after-rotation, 2) add e2e test that rotates token mid-connection, 3) update SDK changelog to recommend new default keepAlive behavior in next release.
Alyssa M: thanks team. I'll send the customer note and close the support escalation once production metrics stable for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
